summary: This article explains how the honey badger, a small member of the weasel family that lives in Africa, Asia, and Saudi Arabia, uses its loose skin, strong claws, venom resistance, and bad smell to survive and raid beehives.
introduce: Show the title “Honey Badgers: Small but Brave” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: an animal that hunts and eats other animals
not easily hurt or changed by something

challengeTerms.def: strong or powerful enough to cause fear or respect
a body feature or behavior that helps a living thing survive where it lives
taking advantage of whatever chances appear, such as any food that is available

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that being brave matters more than being big? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Many people call the honey badger fearless. Do you agree?
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review fearless, predator, and resistant, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses formidable, adaptation, and opportunistic to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
